title: After Testing More Than 50 Pairs of Earbuds, I Finally Found My Favorite
gist: Wired's review of Anker's $170 Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro earbuds (9/10) credits a custom in-house 'Anker Thus AI' compute-in-memory chip for call quality and noise processing that beats pricier AirPods Pro 3 and Bose QuietComfort Ultra rivals, positioning custom silicon as Soundcore's key differentiator against brands using off-the-shelf chips.

insights.claim: The Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro earbuds include a new custom 'Anker Thus AI' chip built by Anker (Soundcore's parent company) using a compute-in-memory design that combines CPU and memory for much greater efficiency, which the reviewer calls a significant investment compared to rivals that use off-the-shelf chips.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Signals Anker/Soundcore is investing in vertical chip design rather than relying on merchant silicon, a strategy that could differentiate its audio products on voice/noise processing and may extend across Anker's broader product line.
insights.quote: this chip is a big investment from the brand compared to using an off-the-shelf option (like many of its rivals do).
insights.locator: paragraph beginning 'Inside the earbuds, there's an even bigger change'

insights.claim: In real-world New York City noise tests (traffic, subway platforms, sirens, cafes), the Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro's call audio quality and background-noise suppression outperformed the Apple AirPods Pro 3, Bose QuietComfort Ultra Earbuds (2nd Gen), and Shokz OpenDots 2.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: A mid-priced earbud beating flagship products from Apple and Bose on call quality is a competitive threat in a segment where those brands command premium pricing.
insights.quote: Apple AirPods Pro 3, Bose QuietComfort Ultra Earbuds (2nd Gen), and Shokz OpenDots 2 sounded bad by comparison.

insights.claim: The Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro is priced at $170, nearly $100 below most of the reviewer's other top-recommended earbuds, while offering noise cancellation just behind only the Bose QuietComfort Ultra Earbuds (2nd Gen) and Sony WF-1000XM6.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Positions Soundcore as a value disruptor able to approach flagship-tier ANC and call performance at a meaningfully lower price point, pressuring premium incumbents on price-performance.
insights.quote: when those are the only complaints I have about earbuds that cost nearly $100 less than most of my other top recommendations, that's a big deal.

insights.claim: The Liberty 5 Pro's default 'Soundcore Signature' sound profile is noticeably bass-heavy out of the box, requiring app-based tuning (Soundcore Balance preset or personalized HearID mode) to sound comparable to Apple or Bose earbuds.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Highlights a real product weakness (reliance on app tuning) that a competitor could exploit by shipping a better-tuned default profile.
insights.quote: It's bass-heavy, so much so that I would bet even an untrained ear would notice the bass boost.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning 'Out of the box, the sound profile'
